name: Ireland (Dublin)
thesis: Grid-only connection is effectively closed around Dublin; viable only with full on-site generation. The clearest hard gate in the set. The outlook is positive only because the 2025 policy reset opened a narrow, self-supply-conditioned path.

latest_action.note: Cost-pillar score now set by one published rule from the delivered-cost band, not by analyst judgement. The band itself is unchanged. PGIQ Rating 32 to 31. Tier 5 Largely closed unchanged.
latest_action.trigger: Cost-pillar scores set from delivered-cost bands by one published rule (cost-rescore-1.1), separate ratings release

pillar_rationale.access: Hard access gate: a 2021-2025 freeze on new Dublin data-center grid connections was lifted in late 2025 only for projects that self-generate or store their full demand. Grid-only connection stays effectively closed in the east.
pillar_rationale.availability: Tight availability: a small, constrained system with data centers already ~22% of national demand.
pillar_rationale.cost: Scored from what a 100 MW load actually pays here once grid fees, taxes and other charges are added, not from the wholesale price: about $150 per MWh (band $130 to $180). On the PGIQ cost scale ($50 per MWh scores 90, $150 per MWh scores 35) that gives 35. At the cheap end of the band it would score 46; at the dear end, 35.
pillar_rationale.momentum: Historically high momentum (a FLAP-D hub), now gated.

realized_cost.basis: USD per MWh recurring, delivered to the standard 100 MW high-load-factor case, excluding customer-funded connection capital and excluding refundable taxes
